q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures.
e: Pure substances have a definite and constant composition, while mixtures do not.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a variable composition.
e: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant composition.

q: John Dalton proposed the theory of matter at the beginning of the 19th century.
e: Dalton proposed that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and indivisible.

q: According to John Dalton, atoms were visible and divisible.
e: John Dalton proposed that atoms were invisible and indivisible.

q: Modern experimental evidence has shown that atoms are indivisible.
e: Modern experimental evidence has shown that atoms are divisible to create either lighter or heavier atoms.

q: The atom is still considered as the basic unit of any element.
e: An atom may combine chemically to form molecules, but the atom remains the basic unit of an element.

q: A molecule is the smallest unit of any substances that possesses the properties of that substance.
e: Molecules can exist in elements as well as compounds.

q: Elements are substances consisting of more than one type of atom.
e: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon atoms.

q: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally.
e: These elements occur naturally, either in the free or combined state.

q: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are liquids.
e: While most elements are solids or gases, mercury and bromine are specifically noted as liquid elements.

q: Metals show metallic luster and have low density.
e: Metals show metallic luster and have high density, whereas non-metals have low density.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile.
e: This is a general property of metals, contrasting with non-metals which are usually brittle.

q: Non-metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.
e: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity.

q: A molecule of an element consists of atoms of the same kind.
e: For example, a hydrogen molecule consists of two atoms of hydrogen.

q: A molecule of a compound consists of more than one kind of atoms combined in a definite ratio.
e: This is the defining characteristic of a molecular compound.

q: An element can be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
e: An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means, whereas a compound can.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not chemically combined.
e: The constituents of a mixture do not combine chemically and are not in fixed ratios.

q: The substances in a mixture are always in fixed ratios.
e: The substances in a mixture are not in fixed ratios, which is why they do not have well-defined specific properties.

q: Stainless steel is an example of a homogeneous solid-solid mixture.
e: Stainless steel is a homogeneous mixture of iron and chromium.

q: Flour and rice powder is an example of a homogeneous solid-solid mixture.
e: Flour and rice powder is an example of a heterogeneous solid-solid mixture.

q: Vinegar is a homogeneous liquid-liquid mixture.
e: Vinegar is a homogeneous mixture of acetic acid and water.

q: Oil and water is an example of a homogeneous liquid-liquid mixture.
e: Oil and water is an example of a heterogeneous liquid-liquid mixture.

q: Air is a homogeneous gas-gas mixture.
e: Air is a homogeneous mixture of different gases including nitrogen, oxygen, argon, and carbon dioxide.

q: Filtration is a method for separating a soluble solid from a liquid.
e: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid.

q: In filtration, the water that passes through the filter paper is called the filtrate.
e: The insoluble solid remains as residue on the filter paper, while the liquid that passes through is the filtrate.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid crystalline state.
e: This is achieved by allowing a hot solution to gradually cool so pure crystals appear.

q: Decanting is just allowing a mixture of solid and liquid or two immiscible liquids to settle and separate by gravity.
e: Decantation is a simple separation process relying on gravity, such as separating wine from sediments.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate components when at least one of them is magnetic in nature.
e: For example, a magnet can be used to attract iron filings from a mixture of sulphur and iron.

q: Simple distillation is used to separate a mixture of two liquids with similar boiling points.
e: Simple distillation is used to separate a solvent from a solution or liquids with different boiling points; fractional distillation is for mixtures of liquids with different boiling points.

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points.
e: It typically uses a fractionating column, such as in the separation of petroleum.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and rotor speed.
e: It is commonly used to separate solids from liquids, such as in milk or blood.

q: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a liquid) and a mobile phase (a solid).
e: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a gas).
